posts.text: @moniquepressleyofficial gives us her thoughts on the James Comey indictment

Kash Patel explains how the criminal investigation into James Comey’s seashell post wasn’t a simple one: This has been a case that's been investigated over the past 9, 10, 11 months. These cases take time. Our investigators work methodically via acyn/X

King Charles: The U.S. Supreme court historical society has calculated that Magna Carta is cited in at least 160 supreme court cases since 1789, not least as the foundation of the principle that executive power is subject to checks and balances. via acyn/X
Blanche says intent is proven through witnesses, documents and defendants’ statements, after Comey said he did not link “86” to harm and removed the post as political speech. Via atrupar / X
Someone needs to tell this administration the origin behind the term "86"...

Rep. McBride: My constituents can’t afford fucking groceries or utility bills, and he now wants to spend taxpayer money on a ballroom? They shouldn’t use a potential tragedy to try to secure funding from taxpayers for the president to have Great Gatsby parties in the White House. via acyn/X
BREAKING NEWS: Dept. of State is finalizing plans to add Donald Trump's face on US passports.
BREAKING NEWS: Former FBI director James Comey is being indicted over a picture he posted online of seashells spelling out "86 47”.
BREAKING NEWS: US gas prices have hit their highest level since the start of the war with Iran... Thoughts?
@Katie Phang: Why can the DOJ break the law, and there are no consequences for it?
